hints: Every path turns around at exactly one node - its highest point. What if you asked, for each node, 'what is the best path whose highest point is here?'
It is the node's value plus the best downward path into its left subtree and the best into its right - taking either only if it helps.
So each node has to report one number upwards: the best path that goes *down* from it, which may use only one of its two sides. And it separately contributes a candidate answer that may use both.
A negative contribution is never worth taking: clamp each side's downward best at zero before adding it.
